atoms.a: In the 1950s, everyone had fridges and freezers.

feedback.end: In the 50s, very few people had fridges or freezers. They kept most of their food in a pantry instead.

atoms.a: This meant that they had to go to the shops more often.

instruction.text: Before supermarkets were invented, there were specific shops for each kind of food. Match the food items to the shops you would buy them in.

b.sound: You would go to the bakery to buy bread, pastries and cakes.
You would go to the butcher’s to buy any meat products.
You would go to the greengrocer’s to buy fruit and vegetables.

feedback.end: In the 50s, you could go to a cobbler, who mended and sold shoes.

instruction.text: Hand the shopping list to the shopkeeper to learn more.

feedback.end: In most shops, you would give your shopping list to the shopkeeper who would gather your shopping and bag it up for you.

instruction.text: You are speaking to Margaret, who is doing her food shopping in the 1950s. Fill in the gaps.
